correctness.rationale: A complete proof for every n≥3: four colours force perfect radius-one codes; binary indicator equations show no code unless n≡2 mod 4; residue colouring attains four when permitted; absence of 4-codes implies an independent-set bound α≤3 for n=8, hence at least six colours; M6 and M8 have complete graph squares; explicitly specified colour words settle n=5,7,8,9,12; four-column duplication and a radius-two three-column locality lemma cover all remaining residues. Both standalone programs verify finite obligations from independent graph constructions, and no bounded finite test is confused with the uniform proof.

originality.rationale: The new statement is the exact square-chromatic number for every Möbius ladder, including five-colour upper constructions and the exceptional six-colour sixteen-vertex instance. Knor and collaborators already proved the underlying perfect-code existence criterion, so that component is not claimed as new. Comparable square-colouring results concern untwisted Cartesian products; strong edge and interval edge colourings concern different invariants. Targeted public-literature and published-record searches returned no theorem implying the full result. Remaining priority risks are explicit.
residual_risks: A complete copy of the 2012 efficient-domination paper was not obtained; only accessible relevant portions were compared. The fact of prior efficient domination is credited.

value.rationale: Square colouring is a standard minimum-separation vertex-colouring invariant relevant to frequency/channel assignment. This result completes it for an infinite natural nonplanar cubic family, separates the perfect-code arithmetic cases from universal five-colourability, explains a distinguished 16-vertex packing obstruction and supplies repeatable constructive optimal patterns. The infinite sharp classification has independent structural content beyond known efficient domination and is not a routine substitution or unmotivated finite census.
